title: a tagged template whose Result is matched discharges the obligation on both the success and the failure side, and the lifted throw arrives as a failure at run time
notes: specification/failures.mdx:136: 'A Result MUST be treated as a must-use value. A source program MUST NOT silently discard a Result without returning, matching, transforming, inspecting, or unwrapping it.' Matching is one of the listed discharges, so a tagged template whose Result is matched is consumed and the program must compile and run. This is the over-correction guard for `a-dropped-result-from-a-tagged-template-is-refused`: that case requires the must-consume rule to start seeing tagged templates as Result producers, and the cheap way to satisfy it is to refuse the SYNTAX rather than the discard. THE SECOND LINE IS THE ONE THAT CARRIES THE WEIGHT. `matchedOnTheFailingSide` passes `bad`, so the tag throws, the throw is lifted into the Result the tag declares, and `boom` is printed by the failure handler. That single word is the evidence for three separate things at once: the tag really ran, its throw really was lifted rather than escaping, and the failure branch really was selected. A backend that recognized the template statically and lowered it to something that does not lift would abort here instead of printing. The first and third lines are the success side reached two ways — matched immediately, and matched after being bound to a `const` — because binding a Result to a local and matching the local is a separate discharge path from matching the producer expression directly. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the failure's identity or message. `04-nominal-errors` owns identity, and this case returns a fixed string from the error handler so that its expectation cannot drift when identity minting changes. It also does not pin postfix `!` propagation of a tagged template's Result, which is a different discharge with its own area. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the second declared stdout line from `boom` to `ok` — which is exactly what this program prints if the tag's throw is NOT lifted into the failure channel and the success branch runs instead — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 806443202078c902912735295c17c0d30bf988b181817e8ee6b3466bace0dbb1 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently).
